chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Salim Abu al-Fadl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a female slave who has a free husband. He said: It is not permissible for anyone to have sexual relations with her until her free husband divorces her.

Therefore, the meaning of this report is that we interpret it to mean that if the buyer agrees to that condition, it is not permissible for anyone [to have relations with her] until she is divorced by the free husband, as detailed in the preceding reports.

key_terms.يَمَسَّهَا: he has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man having relations with a female slave who is married to a free man?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) regarding a female slave (*umm walad* or *mukatab*) married to a free man, establishing that her owner cannot consummate the marriage until her free husband divorces her. This principle, known as *bay' al-umm walad talāquhā* (the sale of the slave entails her divorce), ensures the preservation of her marital bond with her free spouse, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the family unit across social strata. The narration clarifies that this condition applies unless the buyer explicitly waives it, aligning with broader hadith traditions on the legal status of mixed-status marriages.
